title: Joint Detection of Fraud and Concept Drift inOnline Conversations with LLM-Assisted Judgment
abstract: arXiv:2505.07852v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Detecting fake interactions in digital communication platforms remains a challenging and insufficiently addressed problem. These interactions may appear as harmless spam or escalate into sophisticated scam attempts, making it difficult to flag malicious intent early. Traditional detection methods often rely on static anomaly detection techniques that fail to adapt to dynamic conversational shifts. One key limitation is the misinterpretation of benign topic transitions referred to as concept drift as fraudulent behavior, leading to either false alarms or missed threats. We propose a two stage detection framework that first identifies suspicious conversations using a tailored ensemble classification model. To improve the reliability of detection, we incorporate a concept drift analysis step using a One Class Drift Detector (OCDD) to isolate conversational shifts within flagged dialogues. translated_abstract: 检测数字通信平台中的虚假交互仍然是一个具有挑战性且未得到充分解决的问题。这些交互可能表现为无害的垃圾信息，也可能演变为复杂的诈骗企图，使得难以及时识别恶意意图。传统检测方法通常依赖静态异常检测技术，无法适应动态的对话变化。一个关键局限在于将良性话题转换（即概念漂移）误判为欺诈行为，从而导致误报或漏报。我们提出了一个两阶段检测框架，首先使用定制的集成分类模型识别可疑对话。为提高检测的可靠性，我们引入了概念漂移分析步骤，使用单类漂移检测器（OCDD）来分离被标记对话中的对话变化。当检测到漂移时，由大语言模型（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种两阶段检测框架，先通过集成分类模型识别可疑对话，再利用单类漂移检测器区分概念漂移，并结合大语言模型进行辅助判断，从而在在线对话中联合检测欺诈行为，减少将良性话题转变误判为欺诈的误报与漏报。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a two-stage framework that identifies suspicious conversations with an ensemble classifier, isolates concept drift using a One-Class Drift Detector, and applies LLM-assisted judgment to jointly detect fraud while avoiding misinterpreting benign topic shifts as fraudulent behavior.
